text:
Alex Nguyen: heads-up — dashboard alert for /v1/generate p99 just tripped twice in the last 10m. p95 looks normal but p99 is +400ms vs baseline. screenshot: https://redwood-internal.screens/alerts/1897654321.png

Priya Patel: ugh. Is that across all regions or a single endpoint shard?

Alex Nguyen: looks concentrated on prod-us-west-2, but the dashboard rollup shows an odd shape — p50/p95 steady, p99 jumping. Raw spans from traces show a few hosts with long tails.

Marco Diaz: can you paste the prom query you're using for p99? we had past issues where per-host percentiles were computed then averaged which underestimates the true tail.

Alex Nguyen: sure — current panel uses: 
```
max_over_time(histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le,route,instance) (rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[1m]))) [5m:1m])
```
I copied it from the route-breakdown dashboard.

Li Wei: that exact pattern will compute 99th per instance then max them, but if you aggregate incorrectly you can get artefacts. For true cluster p99 you need to merge buckets across instances before quantile. e.g. `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le,route) (rate(...)))` not grouped by instance.

Anne Keller: also worth checking our t-digest rollup job — we downsample tdigest summaries and then compute quantiles on the stored digests. If merging happens in the UI layer (per-host digest -> percentile -> avg) you get a biased result.

Marco Diaz: exactly. TL;DR: two anti-patterns we keep repeating: 1) compute percentile per shard then average, 2) use max_over_time after a per-shard quantile which amplifies transients.

Jon S.: metrics-bot just flagged a config change in rollout-service at 1897654200 (deploy). Could be related: it changed routing policy to split 5% traffic to the new scheduler. metrics-bot: "deploy/rollout-service v2.3.1 — traffic split 95/5"

Priya Patel: if only 5% went to new scheduler why would p99 for the whole route jump? unless the new hosts are causing noisy tails and our aggregation amplifies them.

Alex Nguyen: trace IDs show many of the long requests are from the new scheduler host pool. That explains the host-level tail. But the dashboard shape still looks weird — it's like the p99 metric jumps more than traces indicate.

Li Wei: two quick checks: 1) confirm the dashboard aggregates across instances before quantile (fix query if not). 2) check sample rate and event slicing — if we dropped some fast requests in the sampling then the remaining sample is heavier on slow ones -> p99 skew.

Anne Keller: on the tdigest side, storage downsample window is 1m -> digests get merged every minute. If the new scheduler produces intermittent bursts, merging windows can create artificial spikes in the digest-based quantiles. We should compute quantiles from merged digests not from per-minute percentiles.

Marco Diaz: proposed action items: 
- update dashboard query to sum by (le,route) and recompute (Priya/Alex)
- run a repro locally merging per-instance digests and compute cluster quantiles (Li/Marco)
- add a short-lived per-host tail gauge to detect noisy hosts (Alex)
- revert rollout to 0% if user-facing latency keeps rising (Anne/Jon)

Priya Patel: I'll put up a quick PR to change the Grafana panel and add an annotation for the deploy. PR: https://git.redwood/s/grafana/pulls/432

Jon S.: I'll pause the remainder of the rollout from the console and notify SRE if p99 stays > baseline+200ms for 5m.

Alex Nguyen: updated panel to `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le,route) (increase(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])))` — pushing to staging dashboard now.

metrics-bot: incident-monitor: p99 alert cleared for /v1/generate (1897654460) :white_check_mark:

Li Wei: good catch everyone. Follow-up: we should document guidance in the playbook about "compute cluster quantiles by merging histograms/tdigests before quantile extraction" and add a Grafana lint rule to detect per-instance quantile panels. I'll open a docs PR.

Anne Keller: note for console UX: add a tooltip on route breakdown showing whether a panel is computing cluster-level or shard-level percentiles — saved a few ughs today. :sparkles:

Alex Nguyen: agreed. I'll file a console UX ticket after this thread. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
